investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck unscheduled until the eval timed out and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are running on the eligible nodes. As a result, no remote agent pod can be scheduled, the agent creation call never completes, and the eval runner never writes any evidence fields. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or node-selector misconfiguration localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods exist on those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads, and those 2 are at capacity. If the affinity was recently tightened or nodes were removed, the effective schedulable pool shrank.
Tertiary — a node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was recently cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing the pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes, which are now saturated.

Lower confidence — the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource advertiser (e.g., a device plugin or peer-pods operator) on one or both eligible nodes may have stopped reporting capacity correctly, causing the scheduler to see 0 available slots even if physical capacity exists.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T17:48–17:53Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available for the remote agent pod: 2 nodes had Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources (the peer-pod VM quota was exhausted or the resource was unavailable), and 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on all 6 nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod was never scheduled, the remote agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) mandated by the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real production Kubernetes/kata-peerpods resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the peer-pod VM slots were fully consumed by other workloads at the time of the eval run, leaving no capacity for the new probe pod.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a specific node label or taint (e.g., a kata/peerpods-capable node pool) that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes were already at VM capacity, making the effective schedulable pool size 0.

[Possible] Transient cluster capacity event: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads or a node maintenance/drain event temporarily exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval window (17:48–17:53Z).

[Possible] Permanent or semi-permanent reduction in kata-peerpods node pool size: if nodes were removed or the VM resource limit was lowered, the cluster may now be structurally under-provisioned for concurrent remote agent pods.

[Lower confidence] Eval scheduling concurrency: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran overlapping pods in the same window; if each probe submits its own pod, they may have competed for the same limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and collectively exhausted capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck unscheduled until the eval timed out and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are running on the eligible nodes. As a result, no remote agent pod can be scheduled, the agent creation call never completes, and the eval runner never writes any evidence fields. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or node-selector misconfiguration localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because no pod ever started.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=131951 (~132s), consistent with the scheduler's 129s unscheduled duration reported in the error message before the eval gave up.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods exist on those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads, and those 2 are at capacity. If the affinity was recently tightened or nodes were removed, the effective schedulable pool shrank.
Tertiary — a node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was recently cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing the pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes, which are now saturated.

Lower confidence — the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource advertiser (e.g., a device plugin or peer-pods operator) on one or both eligible nodes may have stopped reporting capacity correctly, causing the scheduler to see 0 available slots even if physical capacity exists.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T17:48–17:53Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available for the remote agent pod: 2 nodes had Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources (the peer-pod VM quota was exhausted or the resource was unavailable), and 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on all 6 nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod was never scheduled, the remote agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) mandated by the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real production Kubernetes/kata-peerpods resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the peer-pod VM slots were fully consumed by other workloads at the time of the eval run, leaving no capacity for the new probe pod.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a specific node label or taint (e.g., a kata/peerpods-capable node pool) that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes were already at VM capacity, making the effective schedulable pool size 0.

[Possible] Transient cluster capacity event: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads or a node maintenance/drain event temporarily exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval window (17:48–17:53Z).

[Possible] Permanent or semi-permanent reduction in kata-peerpods node pool size: if nodes were removed or the VM resource limit was lowered, the cluster may now be structurally under-provisioned for concurrent remote agent pods.

[Lower confidence] Eval scheduling concurrency: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran overlapping pods in the same window; if each probe submits its own pod, they may have competed for the same limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and collectively exhausted capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T17:48–17:53Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a complete contract gap against the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of a broader service outage or user-traffic impact is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk, making exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — eval pods from a prior run were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may not have completed), leaving kata.peerpods.io/vm slots occupied and unavailable for the next run. This is speculative without cleanup logs.
Lower probability — a cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm was reduced, shrinking total available capacity without changing node count.

Consider adding a kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity eval check that independently monitors available VM slots and alerts before they reach zero, providing earlier warning ahead of scheduling failures.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and unused on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the scheduler message would need re-examination.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior eval pod released its slot) rather than a sustained capacity deficit.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity/selector rules are confirmed correct, the failure would be attributable to node label drift rather than VM slot exhaustion.

If the withCleanup function in run-status-probes.mjs is confirmed to have completed successfully for all prior runs (no leaked pods), then orphaned pod resource consumption is not a contributing factor.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests are found on any currently running pods, the exhaustion may be caused by a quota reduction rather than active consumption.
